problem_text:
A logistics manager is selecting cargo containers to load onto a transport vehicle. The available containers are:
* Container 1: weight 32 kg, revenue 254 credits
* Container 2: weight 16 kg, revenue 66 credits
* Container 3: weight 9 kg, revenue 86 credits
* Container 4: weight 47 kg, revenue 148 credits
* Container 5: weight 50 kg, revenue 172 credits
* Container 6: weight 9 kg, revenue 31 credits
* Container 7: weight 37 kg, revenue 266 credits
* Container 8: weight 25 kg, revenue 94 credits
* Container 9: weight 25 kg, revenue 247 credits
* Container 10: weight 3 kg, revenue 141 credits
* Container 11: weight 30 kg, revenue 198 credits
* Container 12: weight 41 kg, revenue 166 credits
* Container 13: weight 25 kg, revenue 231 credits
* Container 14: weight 34 kg, revenue 43 credits
* Container 15: weight 27 kg, revenue 250 credits
* Container 16: weight 48 kg, revenue 165 credits
* Container 17: weight 16 kg, revenue 19 credits
* Container 18: weight 27 kg, revenue 160 credits
* Container 19: weight 39 kg, revenue 239 credits
* Container 20: weight 37 kg, revenue 257 credits
* Container 21: weight 25 kg, revenue 179 credits
* Container 22: weight 47 kg, revenue 189 credits
* Container 23: weight 39 kg, revenue 75 credits
* Container 24: weight 23 kg, revenue 167 credits
* Container 25: weight 37 kg, revenue 245 credits
* Container 26: weight 10 kg, revenue 275 credits
* Container 27: weight 14 kg, revenue 167 credits
* Container 28: weight 6 kg, revenue 244 credits
* Container 29: weight 9 kg, revenue 138 credits
* Container 30: weight 8 kg, revenue 94 credits

The vehicle has a maximum payload capacity of 556 kg. Choose the combination of containers that maximizes total revenue without exceeding this weight limit. Each container must be either fully loaded or left behind.
